reviews.text: This game is a great continuation of an already great series, The new map design, enemies, and loot tables make for a great experience. The improved graphics also make for a new and improved feel from the previous game.

I was so pleased to see that this had come out. I loved RF 3. A lot. However not so much that I would knowingly pay £8 for a game I already own. This game is almost identical to RF3. It even has EXACTLY the same music, sprites and game play. Maybe the tile sets are a little different, but I'm not sure and even then , not enough to make a difference. Same mushrooms potion, founts etc. It's pretty bloody cheeky if you ask me (and you did ask, Steam). I understand that this is early access but making your early access version pretty much just the previous game is bizarre. I understand that maybe the intent is to build on the first game, but if that is so, where it is now is almost entirely identical to RF3. maybe I missed the bit where this state of affairs is explained by the dev/devs. no one one the steam reviews seems to have noticed this, at least they don't mention it. Great game if you've never owned 3 (though 3 is cheaper of course and not early access). Disappointed and annoyed. This feels very scammy. Refund requested.

Healing and summoning enemies were already a problem - some classes just literally cannot get the skills needed to fight through an unlucky group of enemies that had one of each. You can't get to the summoners because of all the ♥♥♥♥ in the way, you can't chip them down and kite because they constantly get healed, and you cannot make progress since the only things you can kill are the summons, which are on a lower cooldown than you can possibly deal with. It was a ♥♥♥♥♥♥ spot of rng that just wrecked some runs. Then they just patched it yesterday so that summoners summon MORE often, and healers heal MORE often. It's just over the top. Some class / race combinations will lose a run they are dominating out of nowhere, just by hitting the wrong batch of enemies even once. It's a total RNG fest now, very little skill involved. Basically, there was already a huge problem in game design, which instead of fixing, they actively went out of their way to make it even worse. It's pretty tone-deaf development. If they're too blind to realize these things needed tuned DOWN, not cranked to 11, then I have little hope that this game will ever improve.

Tl;dr just play Rogue Fable III lol. I cannot recommend this game at all. What started out as an approachable game has become a nightmare slog as the developer keeps making tedious 'balance' changes. A few examples from past 'fixes' 'Remove a single starting talent from each class (more varied builds based on dungeon drops)' meaning that if you relied on said talent you are forced to pray to the RNG in hopes that it will be kind to you. Multiple times have I gone in with a class and found a tome that offered only talents that didn't benefit the build I was going for. In regards to the duelist: 'Lunge (Damage): removed as I don't want him to even have the option of maxing damage with his core talents.' Like, what even is this? Why play a class that has weaker damage? Just play a barbarian with charge at this point. Sure, there is the talent disengage which relies on spd points you could use to attack and back off except: 'Speed Points: Reduced many items that had 2SP to 1SP. I think Speed Points should be harder to stack up, similar to Block Points. Based on my own testing this mostly just means that characters that previously would hit 7-8SP now end up with something like 5-6SP which is still plenty.' And, 'Athletics: 2SP => 1SP on the base talent. Similar to the change to items I feel it should not be so easy to stack a ton of SP.' Cool, so now if I want to have a Str based character and want to use spd I have to waste a bunch of resources and or item slots instead of using one item or one lucky athletics find. And you ABSOLUTELY need spd points in this game, it's the only way to avoid most of the ways to die. The trade off shouldn't be nerfing your ability to do damage to actually kill the monsters before they lightning or summon you to death. Also, removed from the last game: Talent Fountains, Attribute Fountains, Wells of Wishing, Enchantment Tables, keys. And rooms for gold, potions, scrolls, food All in favor of Crystal Chest rooms because praise 'choice' over interesting/useful. This game is tedious, frustrating, and clearly going to get worse as the dev keeps doing their best to 'balance' the game. What a waste of time this whole experience was, please don't make the same mistake I did.

I only have a few hours; but I'm coming from playing Rogue Fable III quite a bit. If you own Rogue Fable III, the improvements here are smaller than a usual sequel, but the new tiles and some functionalities are nice. It's in a perfect place between a rogue-lite and a full on old-school dungeon crawler. The stats are simple, clearly defined integers and what items and abilities do is easy to understand. However, all sorts of unexpected situations arise from the many environmental hazards, unique attacks and enemy types. Unusual for a traditional roguelike, the game is very fast paced. Every class having a dash adds a lot of fun; even as a necromancer you'll find yourself dodging spells and luring enemies into exploding mushrooms. It's easy to pick up, difficult to beat but never feels punishing. As for balance and whatnot, I'm not one for that kind of thing; however, I can naively say that I continue to play without issue. From Rogue Fable III to every update so far in IV there hasn't been anything keeping me from coming back. I would also say this is the only such game I've gotten more mainstream gaming friends to play.
